structured_result.summary: CODEX predicts a qualified yes: mobile should be conversation-first as the attention and decision layer, with durable multi-agent views behind a top menu, only approval and blocker interruptions in conversation, and raw xterm reserved for desktop. This requires persistent current-state, ownership, consent, reattach, and evidence affordances; it is not a claim of meeting consensus.

meeting_dissent=D8: advancing with 2/3 meeting reviewers absent is not a full cross-review.

paths.label: qualified conversation-first
paths.prediction: Use conversation as the mobile entry and attention layer. Keep ordinary progress out of the transcript and surface only approval or blocker interruptions, with a compact current-run indicator and direct re-entry path.
required_guards: Current run, owner, mode, last change, and action-required state remain visible without reading the transcript.
A returning user can recover what changed and reattach without guessing identity.
Approval cards expose context, consequence, expiry, and refusal or defer paths.

paths.label: menu-backed durable control plane
paths.prediction: Put fleet, galaxy, rooms, durable status, evidence, and handoff views behind a top menu. The menu is the place to inspect shared state and switch context; conversation is not the sole source of truth.
required_guards: The menu exposes unread exceptions, stale ownership, and active blockers at a glance.
Navigation preserves the selected run and room context.
Normal progress is distinguishable from demand-for-action.

paths.label: desktop-mobile capability split
paths.prediction: Reserve raw xterm for desktop. Mobile supports bounded inspection, approval or denial, defer, stop, reattach, and escalation, then hands off to desktop for shell authoring, deep evidence, and recovery.
required_guards: Desktop and mobile share stable run identity and evidence lineage.
Handoff confirms the target context and current state.
Mobile cannot silently broaden authority through a notification or chat reply.

paths.label: conditional high-concurrency fallback
paths.prediction: If testing shows missed state or approval errors, make the active multi-agent operation view the default for high-concurrency contexts while retaining conversation as the exception and explanation layer. This is a fallback hypothesis, not the primary recommendation.
paths.trigger: Repeated failure to locate ownership, blockers, or changed-since-last-view state within a short glance interaction.

challenge_to_conversation_first_ui.challenge: A conversation transcript can become the apparent control plane even though long-running work is parallel, asynchronous, mode-sensitive, and evidence-heavy. Hiding durable state behind a menu can produce missed ownership changes, stale approvals, and poor recovery after absence.
challenge_to_conversation_first_ui.discriminating_test: After a 30-minute absence, users must identify current owner, mode, last meaningful change, and required action within 10 seconds without searching the transcript.

risks.risk: Hidden mode, authority, or ownership creates a cockpit-style mode error.
risks.mitigation: Keep mode, owner, currentness, and action-required state visible in the run header and menu badges.

risks.risk: Notification and approval fatigue causes missed or accidental consent.
risks.mitigation: Separate status from demand-for-action and test distinct interrupt, inbox, and silent-consent grains.

risks.risk: A persuasive summary is mistaken for an audit trail.
risks.mitigation: Provide faithful event evidence, provenance, drilldown, override, and recovery paths.

risks.risk: Reattach or handoff resumes the wrong run or loses responsibility.
risks.mitigation: Use stable run identity, explicit ownership transfer, readback, and last-observed state.

risks.risk: Serial and accessibility users lose asynchronous changes in a linear stream.
risks.mitigation: Offer changed-since-last-view summaries, recoverable focus, and announced exception state.

basis: The frozen CODEX pack directly supports detach and reattach, explicit consent, evidence, shared state, and desktop-mobile handoff.
The meeting found derived-field convergence stronger than exemplar unanimity.
The direct conversation lineage is missing across all 51 seeds, and D8 records an incomplete cross-review.
The 17-seed coverage floor makes broad exemplar agreement weak corroboration.

unresolved_dissent.implication: The prediction lacks a completed independent cross-review because CODEX and GROK meeting rounds failed.
Exemplar convergence may be a method artifact; derived-field convergence should carry more weight.
The meeting did not establish whether conversation should be the mobile default because the relevant conversation lineage is absent.
Uncertainty labels are not fully comparable across packs.
They remain hypotheses and must not be treated as consensus architecture.

smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.scenario: Run several agents with one silent completion, one retry, one blocker, and one approval request.
measure: time to identify owner and current state

smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.comparison: Approval or blocker cards in conversation versus push notification plus inbox or menu badge.
smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.scenario: Vary urgency, consequence, expiry, and available defer or deny actions.

smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.comparison: Mobile bounded controls followed by desktop xterm handoff versus attempting equivalent work through mobile conversation.
smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.scenario: Inspect evidence, stop or reattach a long-running run, then continue on desktop.

smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.comparison: Transcript-only recovery versus changed-since-last-view summary with linear navigation.
smallest_discriminating_prototypes_or_us.scenario: A screen-reader user returns after multiple asynchronous events.
